chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Ihram from Ghamra. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it if one enters into Ihram from it, and Bareed al-Aqee al-Aqeeq was more beloved to me (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.بَرِيدُ الْعَقِيقِ: Bareedee al-Aqeeq, a specific location in the valley of Aqeeq, preferred by the Imam
key_terms.غَمْرَةَ: Ghamra, a place near Mecca used as a miqat
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Where is it permissible to enter Ihram from according to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the flexibility of Miqat locations, affirming that while entering Ihram from Ghamra is legally valid, Imam al-Rida (AS) expressed a personal preference for Bareed al-Aqeeq. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of the difference between obligatory rulings (wajib) and recommended preferences (mustahabb) in ritual practice. It underscores the principle that while the minimum boundary is sufficient, choosing a location closer to the sacred city can enhance the spiritual experience of the pilgrim.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan BinYahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about (wearing) the Ihraam from Ghamra. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it if one wears Ihraam from it, and Bareyd Al-Aqeeq would be more beloved to measws’.
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about assuming the state of Ihram from Ghamrah.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful, but Barid al-‘Aqiq is more desirable to me.’”
